decisions.description: The twenty percent budget cut is projected to run for about three months

actions.description: Send Ron the full budget numbers report for every department
Each department names three specific items it can cut to reach the reduction

risks.description: A three-month estimate for the cut is likely to turn into five months
Beth's department is already scraping its budget and may not be able to cut twenty percent at all
Rachel's department cannot go below two million without the operation failing
Cost estimates on this project have historically come in at two to four times what was anticipated

open_questions.description: Whether cuts should follow a hierarchy of what matters most rather than a flat twenty percent from every department
How much revenue the aquarium will actually bring in, which will not be known for two months

notes: The twenty percent cut itself is NOT recorded as a decision. Ron arrives with it and Rachel confirms 'there is no way back on the twenty percent' -- it is handed down, not settled here, the same reading applied to the finance briefings in tiron-TS3003a-c01 and tiron-ES2004a-c01. What this meeting does settle is the duration, which Ron gives only when Beth asks. Sarah's 'for tomorrow' (seg-0087) is another relative deadline that stays null. The three-items-to-cut instruction is recorded as an action rather than a decision, so the same instruction is not counted twice under two kinds.
